name: Carmelite mendicant rule approved
summary: Innocent IV's bull Quae honorem Conditoris (1 October 1247) mitigates Albert of Jerusalem's primitive eremitic rule, permitting Carmelite friars to settle in towns and beg for alms, formally folding the order into the mendicant family alongside Dominicans and Franciscans.

_quarry.structural_significance: Completes the 13th-century mendicant constellation (with Augustinian Hermits added 1256); the Carmelite scapular and Marian devotion become major pillars of late-medieval lay piety.
